builder_plan.scenario: A self-hosted model uses more compute or memory than your workload can justify.
builder_plan.change: Check for a usable pruned checkpoint and runtime support before attempting model surgery.
builder_plan.baseline: The original unpruned model at the same precision, context, and load.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Task quality, actual GPU memory, serving throughput, and preparation cost.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: SLICEChat: Progressive In-Encoder Token Pruning for Whole-Slide Pathology Language Models
summary: Replaces the standard pipeline of encoding thousands of WSI patch tokens and compressing only after slide encoding with progressive language-supervised, region-aware token pruning inside a hybrid Mamba-Transformer encoder before multimodal fusion. The cost is a custom encoder, pruning schedule, supervised pruning signal, and added training and validation complexity rather than a drop-in inference optimization. It can fail through removal of diagnostically relevant regions, sensitivity to keep-rate and cohort shift, and benchmark gains that may not transfer to a different pathology stack.
rationale: This is a domain-specific whole-slide pathology MLLM design that requires encoder-level modification and validation, so it is relevant to constrained infrastructure mainly as an option to monitor unless the team already deploys WSI pathology models.
technique: Progressive in-encoder token pruning for WSI MLLMs

claims.statement: Replaces the standard pipeline of encoding thousands of WSI patch tokens and compressing only after slide encoding with progressive language-supervised, region-aware token pruning inside a hybrid Mamba-Transformer encoder before multimodal fusion. The cost is a custom encoder, pruning schedule, supervised pruning signal, and added training and validation complexity rather than a drop-in inference optimization. It can fail through removal of diagnostically relevant regions, sensitivity to keep-rate and cohort shift, and benchmark gains that may not transfer to a different pathology stack.

Reports 79.84% accuracy on TCGA and 59.09% on BCNB in SlideBench VQA, outperforming prior slide-level pathology MLLMs, with the highest overall WSI-Bench metrics; memory and latency are described as competitive but not quantified.
